consensus_summary: Pearl primarily symbolizes the kingdom of heaven (or by extension salvation/Christ/the gospel) as a treasure of supreme value worth surrendering all to obtain, from the Parable of the Pearl of Great Price; alternatives include Christ or the church as the pearl, sacred truths (Matt 7:6), New Jerusalem glory (Rev 21:21), or negative luxury.
book_summary: Pearl is the one complete light: under KJV rubies (peninim = pearl), wisdom and the bride are priced above pearls; the night sky's one pearl is the full moon (keseh = fulness), governor of appointed times; the one-pearl gates are the merchant's entry at the King's gate.
consensus_core_identification: kingdom of heaven (supreme-value treasure from Matt 13:45-46), with common variants Christ or church
book_core_identification: full moon as the night sky's one pearl / the one complete light (with wisdom/bride priced above and pearl gates as merchant entry)
boundary_disagreement: Book introduces full-moon / appointed-times / one-complete-light lunar symbolism wholly absent from consensus; retains only the peripheral one-pearl gates and merchant allusion while centering an unrelated celestial referent.
material_contradiction: None explicit; the entry's common-view note separately acknowledges the kingdom/church reading without rejecting it, so the novel lunar core does not directly negate the consensus referent.
rationale: Consensus cores (and all listed alternatives) uniformly orbit the Matthean parable's pearl as kingdom/Christ/church/supreme treasure or related applications (sacred truth, glory, luxury). The book's minimum core—the full moon as 'the one pearl' via keseh wordplay, linked to wisdom/bride and calendrical governance—has no counterpart in any consensus response. Shared surface elements (Rev 21:21 gates, merchant) are secondary and do not preserve or refine the central identification, producing novelty by absence rather than refinement or contradiction.
strongest_objection: The full-moon equation rests on specialized Hebrew letter/word associations (keseh under throne/time-appointed, peninim) not recoverable from the plain sense of the printed verses alone, which mainstream symbolism never links to pearl.
